messages:
kevin-support: FYI customer 'AcmePay' opened a ticket for a massive KMS billing spike overnight (~120k Decrypt attempts in ~2h). Quick triage shows repeated Decrypts with missing/\"null\" EncryptionContext and our proxy retries are amplifying things. Dropping some log samples and notes.

kevin-support: ```
2026-03-16T01:12:02Z INFO request_id=abc123 proxied_decrypt key=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/abcd encryption_context=\"\" -> 200
2026-03-16T01:12:03Z INFO request_id=abc124 proxied_decrypt key=arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/abcd encryption_context=null -> 400 KMS.InvalidCiphertextException
2026-03-16T01:12:03Z INFO request_id=abc125 proxy-retry attempt=1 original_request_id=abc124
2026-03-16T01:12:04Z INFO request_id=abc126 proxy-retry attempt=2 original_request_id=abc124
... repeated hundreds/minute for same original_request_id
```

maria-sec: Can you attach raw HTTP bodies for a couple failing correlation ids + the X-Correlation-Id captured? Are these routed through kms-proxy or going straight to AWS? tagging @ops-oncall

kevin-support: All via kms-proxy. Correlation ids: abc124, abc198, abc402. Raw request example shows client sent EncryptionContext: null (JS/JSON), proxy forwards a trimmed header sometimes and KMS returns 400. Our retry layer then retries. Raw HTTP snippet below.

kevin-support: ```
POST /decrypt HTTP/1.1
Host: kms-proxy.internal
X-Correlation-Id: abc124
Authorization: AWS4-HMAC-SHA256 ...
Content-Type: application/json

{"CiphertextBlob":"..base64..","EncryptionContext":null}
```

raj-eng: I repro'd locally with java-sdk v1.11 and an older proxy client. The problem: our proxy's retry middleware only treated 5xx as terminal, so it classified some 4xx (KMS.InvalidCiphertextException) as retryable in the chain. Node repro snippet:

raj-eng: ```js
// simplified repro
await retry(async () => {
  return await kms.decrypt({CiphertextBlob, EncryptionContext: undefined}).promise();
}, {retries: 5, retryOn: (err) => err.statusCode >= 500});
// because retryOn ignores 4xx we loop on 400s returned by KMS proxy
```

kms-proxy-bot: kms-proxy: observed 12,300 proxied failures in window 2026-03-16T01:00:00Z-03:00:00Z. Top key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/abcd. sample-correlation: abc124

ops-oncall: Immediate mitigations proposed:
- tell support to instruct customer to disable SDK client-side retries for Decrypt (short-term)
- hotfix proxy to treat KMS 4xx as terminal and stop requeuing
- add short dedupe/rate-limit for identical Decrypt(key+ciphertext+ctx) to prevent retry storms
I'll open an incident ticket and get refunds on the table after we confirm counts.

maria-sec: CloudTrail looks odd: many Decrypt events from the abc124 window are missing. Some requests either never reached AWS or were swallowed in the proxy. We need to map proxy internal ids to aws-request-id for audit/compliance. If proxy forwarded a request we should have an aws-request-id in logs; grep for aws-req-id.

kevin-support: Grepped: many abc124 traces show "proxy-internal-id=abc125 retry=1 -> no aws-req-id". So several retry attempts never reached KMS which explains CloudTrail gaps but we still counted them in our internal metering because we bill per proxied attempt.

raj-eng: Root cause hypothesis: 1) client sent EncryptionContext=null (some SDKs serialize missing ctx as null), 2) proxy normalizes that to empty string in some code paths, leading to KMS returning 400 (InvalidCiphertext), 3) our proxy retry middleware incorrectly treats certain 4xx as transient -> retries -> storm. Combined with customer-side retries results in massive amplification.

raj-eng: Proposed fix plan:
- change proxy retry policy: treat explicit KMS 4xx (InvalidCiphertext, AccessDenied, NotFound) as terminal and return original 4xx to client
- mark proxy-side errors that occurred pre-forward (no aws-req-id) as non-billable temporarily and backfill audit once we map events
- implement short dedupe token (hash(key+ciphertext+encctx)) with 1s window to squash duplicates

ops-oncall: Action items (owners + ETA):
- raj-eng: implement proxy 4xx terminal behavior + dedupe (ETA: EOD today)
- ops-oncall: add temporary rate-limit on key arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111:key/abcd and file incident INC-2026-314
- kevin-support: notify account teams and prepare refund estimate and KB
- maria-sec: run audit mapping to confirm which attempts reached AWS vs which were internal-only

kevin-support: Customer-facing KB repro steps (for accounts):
1) use java-sdk v1.11 (or older) with default retry config
2) call Decrypt with null or omitted EncryptionContext
3) induce a short network hiccup between proxy and AWS KMS or a transient 5xx from the proxy
4) observe client-side retry loop causing proxy to re-attempt; if proxy also retries on certain 4xx you can get a multiplier effect

maria-sec: For the RCA we need a timeline, counts (total proxied attempts, forwarded attempts with aws-request-id, successful decrypts, failed terminal 4xx counts), and confirmation that no plaintext was exfiltrated. From initial logs none of the failed/de-duped attempts produced successful plaintext responses. Also need to document CloudTrail gaps caused by proxy swallowing forward attempts.

raj-eng: I'll push a small patch to the proxy today (PR + changelog) and cut a canary to staging. Will post PR link and staging canary metrics here. Owning the fix.

ops-oncall: Opening INC-2026-314 now and assigning pagers. I'll update the account team with preliminary numbers and mark billing hold for suspected non-forwarded attempts. Thanks all. :white_check_mark:
